purpose: Guide a narrow human-confirmation pass across the frozen representative full-application workflows without reopening route scope or re-proving backend truth already owned by automation.

reviewModeDefinitions.human-judgment-with-automation-guardrail: Human observation is the primary review signal, while the representative Playwright workflow remains the guardrail for backend truth and route correctness.
reviewModeDefinitions.helper-supported: Use the listed read-only helper only when the UI alone does not make the current session or dev-inbox state sufficiently clear.

classificationBuckets.Defect: The observed behavior conflicts with an accepted requirement, established baseline, or clear workflow expectation.
classificationBuckets.Acceptable Difference: The observed behavior differs from reviewer preference or expectation but does not justify remediation inside the current baseline.
classificationBuckets.Deferred Follow-up: The observation is real or potentially valuable, but the proper owner is outside this set or the work is too broad for the current UAT lane.

severityScale.Critical: Blocks sign-in, navigation, or a core success path inside the frozen workflow subset.
severityScale.Major: Materially harms clarity, trust, or successful completion of a selected workflow and should be remediated before closeout unless the project lead accepts a written deferral.
severityScale.Minor: Noticeable issue with a reasonable workaround that does not break the workflow.
severityScale.Trivial: Cosmetic or extremely low-impact issue recorded for completeness.

deferRules.observationType: Backend truth, persistence, or mutating correctness already covered by representative Playwright workflows
Broad exploratory regression testing outside the five frozen workflow IDs
Broader accessibility recertification work without a concrete workflow-blocking observation
deferRules.owner: Completed accessibility-and-stubbing baseline or later accessibility follow-up

deferRules.observationType: Documentation or packaging changes not directly justified by a confirmed UAT finding

items.title: Product availability toggle remains understandable and trustworthy
steps: Sign in through the seeded-session helper as admin@acmecoffee.com.
Open /admin/products and search for Blonde Roast - Decaf - Espresso.
Toggle the product availability once, observe the immediate page state, then restore the original state before moving on.
guardrailSignals: The Product Administration heading and the target row remain reachable without access-denied fallback.
A state-change message appears after the toggle and the switch reflects the changed state.
Representative automation already proves the mutation path and backend restore behavior.
humanObservationFocus: The toggle control makes its current state obvious before and after the click.
The feedback around the state change feels trustworthy rather than delayed, ambiguous, or noisy.
The resulting row and page state stay easy to read after the mutation.

items.title: Add-product dialog layout, validation copy, and keyboard path feel coherent
steps: Stay signed in as admin@acmecoffee.com and open /admin/products.
Open the Add Product dialog.
Attempt one invalid submit path so the validation messaging becomes visible.
Complete the form using the keyboard as much as practical, create one product successfully, then archive the created product if you use a real new record.
guardrailSignals: The dialog opens from the admin products route and blocks the invalid submit path.
The Create action becomes enabled only after the required fields are valid.
Representative automation already proves one successful product creation and cleanup path.
humanObservationFocus: The dialog layout feels organized and readable instead of cramped or visually confusing.
Validation copy explains what needs to change without forcing guesswork.
The focus path and keyboard flow feel intentional from field to field and into the Create action.

items.title: Organization switch makes the active customer scope obvious and later denial trustworthy
steps: Sign in through the seeded-session helper as casey.hart@acmecoffee.com.
Open /customers while still in the internal organization.
Use the shell Switch org control to move into the retail-business customer scope.
Confirm /orders remains reachable in the switched customer scope.
Open /admin/users and observe the denial state.
guardrailSignals: The active-organization label changes after the switch.
Orders stays reachable in the customer scope before the later denial check.
Representative automation already proves that the switched session loses the internal route and cannot access /admin/users.
humanObservationFocus: The shell makes the active organization obvious after the scope switch.
The transition from internal to customer scope feels trustworthy instead of disorienting.
The later denial state reads as an expected permission boundary, not a broken page.

items.persona: Regional sales rep with scoped BackofficeUserAdmin authority
items.title: Scoped admin warning and post-switch banner stay clearly tied to the active organization
steps: Sign in through the seeded-session helper as sloane.reyes@acmecoffee.com.
Open /admin/users before choosing a manageable organization.
Read the warning state, then switch into one managed retail organization.
Open /admin/users again and observe the scoped admin banner plus one available grant or revoke action.
guardrailSignals: The initial /admin/users route shows the user-admin scope warning.
After the switch, the admin scope banner includes the managed organization name.
Representative automation already proves one scoped admin action and verifies the permission does not leak across organizations.
humanObservationFocus: The initial warning clearly explains why actions are blocked before a manageable organization is selected.
The scoped admin banner stays visibly tied to the active organization after the switch.
The follow-on action remains understandable as organization-scoped rather than global.

items.title: Real magic-link sign-in remains clear end to end for the customer orders journey
steps: Clear prior dev-inbox links for james.smith@example.com before starting the workflow.
Open /login and request a sign-in link for james.smith@example.com.
Review the on-page confirmation state before opening the captured magic link.
Complete the magic-link sign-in and land on /orders.
Open one visible order detail page and confirm the signed-in customer flow remains coherent.
guardrailSignals: The sign-in request produces a dev-captured magic link and the completion path lands in the signed-in shell.
Orders is reachable in the customer scope and one visible order detail page opens successfully.
Representative automation already proves the signed-in order-detail path and the blocked foreign-order branch.
humanObservationFocus: The login form, confirmation copy, and overall sign-in messaging make the next step obvious before the magic link is opened.
The full magic-link journey feels coherent rather than technical or confusing.
The signed-in orders flow still feels clearly customer-scoped after sign-in completes.
